findings.issue: The bound `‖(t:𝕜) • v‖ ≤ ‖v‖` for `t ∈ Icc 0 1` is proved twice: in `hL1` (line 54, `rw [hLapply, norm_smul, RCLike.norm_ofReal, abs_of_nonneg ht.1, one_mul]`) and again in `hmem` (lines 63-64, a 7-lemma `rw` chain through `dist_eq_norm`, `add_sub_cancel_left`, `norm_smul`, ...). findings.fix: Prove it with `by simp [hL]` (this uses `ContinuousLinearMap.smul_apply` and `ContinuousLinearMap.id_apply`), or add a comment explaining why `rfl` is intended.
findings.issue: `hLapply (t) (v) : L t v = (t : 𝕜) • v := rfl` relies on unfolding the coercion of `(t:𝕜) • ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 E` to a function. That is definitional equality across the ContinuousLinearMap wrapper, with no comment explaining it.

summary: Proofs are mostly robust; the Hadamard lemma repeats one norm estimate as two long rewrite chains that will break on Mathlib renames, and proves `hLapply` with an undocumented `rfl` that depends on definitional equality.
